ActionCall.description:
The body of ``POST /api/plugins/{wf}/actions/{name}`` (08 §Plugins).

``input`` is whatever the action's form produced, and it is
validated against the action's own model on arrival rather than
described here: the model is the plugin's, so no schema this
application generates could name it (09 §Declarations, "the model
**is** the form"). An action that declares none takes none, and
whatever was sent is ignored.

input.description: The form's value. Validated against the action's model; a misfit is the 422 of 08 §Conventions, naming each field.
input.title: Input

scope.description: The ids the handler's context is resolved from.

ActionCall.title: ActionCall

ActionOut.description: One action of the manifest, and the form the SPA renders for it.

confirm.description: Whether the SPA asks for confirmation before calling it.
confirm.title: Confirm

name.description: The action's name, as its URL spells it.
name.title: Name

schema.description: JSON Schema of the input model — the form itself.
schema.title: Schema

scope.description: What has to be resolved before it can run.

title.description: What the button and the palette entry say.
title.title: Title

ActionOut.title: ActionOut

ActionScope.description:
Where an action was invoked (08 §Plugins, 09 §Context and scopes).

The three ids a plugin *route* reads off its query string, sent in
the body because an action is a ``POST``. All three are optional
here: what an action needs resolved is the ``scope`` it declared,
and :func:`mount_actions` is what holds the body to it.

node.description: The node the action was invoked on.
node.title: Node

run_id.description: The run the action was invoked on.
run_id.title: Run Id

task_id.description: The attempt the action was invoked on.
task_id.title: Task Id

ActionScope.title: ActionScope

AgentStats.description:
The stats entry of 05 §Stats entry verbatim.

Every measurement is optional because 05 omits what it cannot
determine rather than zero-filling it (01 §Real data only).
AgentStats.title: AgentStats

AgentTask.description:
One attempt as the agent running it sees it (08 §Agent-facing).

The identity of the attempt, the run's title and description, the
payload the node was called with, and the work log that is the
inter-stage channel (D4). Everything an agent needs to start, and
nothing an operator route would add.

attempt.description: Which attempt of this node this is, from 1.
attempt.title: Attempt

description.description: The operator's longer brief for the run.
description.title: Description

input.description: The payload the node was enqueued with; null when it had none.
input.title: Input

log.description: The run's work log, oldest first and never truncated, without the `stats` entries.
log.title: Log

output_schema.description: The JSON Schema a submission must fit, when the agent façade running this attempt declared an `output_model`.
output_schema.title: Output Schema

run_id.description: The run the attempt belongs to.
run_id.title: Run Id

task_id.description: This attempt's id; the one the token is for.
task_id.title: Task Id

title.description: The operator's title for the run.
title.title: Title

AgentTask.title: AgentTask

Answer.description:
Answer a request (`POST /api/requests/{id}/answer`, 06 §The model).

``option_id`` for an ``options`` request and ``value`` for a ``text``
or ``form`` one. Both are optional here because ``value`` may
legitimately be any JSON — including ``null``, which is why "which one
was given" cannot be decided by looking at the values alone: the
request's own ``mode`` decides, and the request service refuses the
mismatch with the error code 06 §Errors names for it.

option_id.description: The chosen option, for an `options` request.
option_id.title: Option Id

value.description: The answer, for a `text` or `form` request.
value.title: Value

Answer.title: Answer

AnswerAuthor.description:
Who answered. ``engine`` is a headless fallback: a permission
timeout action or a declined elicitation (06 §Timeouts).
AnswerAuthor.title: AnswerAuthor

AnswerPoll.description:
The result of one long-poll (`GET …/requests/{rid}`, 06 §Surfaces).

``answered`` is the field to branch on. Until it is true the other
two are absent, because a request with no answer has no author
either; once it is true ``answer`` is the chosen ``option_id`` of an
``options`` request and the value of a ``text`` or ``form`` one —
the same folding :class:`~athanore.store.rows.RequestView` does, so
an operator reading the request and the agent reading its answer see
the same value.

Re-delivery is idempotent: nothing is claimed by a poll, so an agent
that lost a response and asked again gets the same answer again.

answer.description: The chosen `option_id`, or the value of a `text` or `form` answer. Null before an answer, and for an answer that was null.
answer.title: Answer

answered.description: Whether an answer has been recorded.
answered.title: Answered

answered_by.description: Who answered: the operator, or the engine on a headless fallback. Null until answered.

AnswerPoll.title: AnswerPoll

ApiError.description:
The body of every refusal: ``{error, code, ...extras}``.

``code`` is the :class:`~athanore.api.errors.ErrorCode` vocabulary,
referenced rather than inlined, which is how the SPA gets a union
instead of a bare string (08 §OpenAPI). ``errors`` is the extra a
validation failure and a rejected submission carry, and it is 18's
:class:`~athanore.events.payloads.ValidationError` rather than a
second model of the same three fields: one function
(:func:`~athanore.agents.submissions.validate_submission`) projects
pydantic's errors onto ``loc``/``msg``/``type``, and the list it
returns is what the 422 body carries *and* what ``submission.rejected``
publishes. The rest of 08's "...extras" are open, so the schema allows
further properties rather than pretending the two named fields are all
a body can hold.

code.description: The stable code a client branches on; the wording of `error` may change, this may not.

error.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.
error.title: Error

errors.description: Per-field detail, on a validation failure or a rejected submission. Absent otherwise.
errors.title: Errors

ApiError.title: ApiError

Arrivals.description:
How much of an open fan-out has reached a join (04 §Fan-in).

The innermost pending fan-out, which is the one the operator is
waiting on; the SPA renders it as `2 of 3 arrived` (10 §Graph pane).

arrived.description: Branches that have reached the join.
arrived.title: Arrived

Arrivals.title: Arrivals

Ask.description:
A question an agent puts to the operator (`POST …/ask`, 06).

``schema`` is spelled ``schema_`` in Python, as it is in
:class:`~athanore.api.schemas.requests.RequestView`, and keeps
``schema`` as its alias — the name 08 and the curl line of 19 fix on
the wire.

options.description: The choices, for a pick-one question. A bare string is an option that is its own id and label.
options.title: Options

prompt.description: The question, as the operator will read it.
prompt.title: Prompt

schema.description: A JSON Schema the answer must fit, for a form question.
schema.title: Schema

Ask.title: Ask

AskOption.description:
One choice an agent offers the operator (08 §Agent-facing).

``option_id`` is what an answer names and what comes back from the
long-poll; ``name`` is what the operator is shown and defaults to the
id, which is what a bare string in ``options`` is short for.

kind.description: A label for the option; carried through as given.
kind.title: Kind

name.description: What to show the operator; the `option_id` when omitted.
name.title: Name

AskOption.title: AskOption

AskOut.description:
The request an ask opened (08 §Agent-facing).

``mode`` is reported back because the agent did not choose it
directly: it sent options, a schema or neither, and this is what that
was read as — which is also what tells it what shape of answer to
expect from the long-poll.

mode.description: The shape of the answer expected.

request_id.description: The id to poll for an answer.
request_id.title: Request Id

AskOut.title: AskOut

BranchRef.description:
Which branch an output came out of (D58).

The index and the key of each frame, and not the frame's ``fanout`` or
``count``: an output names its branch so a consumer can group by it,
and the task it came from is in the same entry for anything more.

index.description: The branch's zero-based index in its fan-out.
index.title: Index

key.description: The payload that branch was given.
key.title: Key

BranchRef.title: BranchRef

ChunkKind.description:
The kinds of the agent transcript (05 §The ACP client).

``text`` and ``thought`` are the assistant's message and reasoning
chunks, ``tool_call``/``tool_result`` the ACP tool updates, ``notice``
a line the façade itself wrote.
ChunkKind.title: ChunkKind

run_id.description: The id of the run that was queued.
run_id.title: Run Id

EdgeKind.description: What kind of edge one node's arrow to another is (08 §Graph semantics).
EdgeKind.title: EdgeKind

EditRun.description:
Change a run's title, its description, or both (`PATCH /api/runs/{id}`).

Both fields are optional and a field that is absent is left alone —
which is why they are optional rather than defaulted: an edit that
sent no description must not blank one. An edit that names neither is
accepted and changes nothing, which is what ``Ops.edit`` does with it:
a patch is not the place to refuse a caller for being redundant.
EditRun.title: EditRun

EngineRecovered.description: Rows reset to ``ready`` at startup. No ``run_id``.
EngineRecovered.title: EngineRecovered

EngineStopping.description: Attempts interrupted by a shutdown (04 §Shutdown). No ``run_id``.
EngineStopping.title: EngineStopping

ErrorCode.description:
The stable ``code`` of an error body — 08 §Conventions, in full.

A code is a contract with the SPA and the CLI: it is what a client
branches on, so it outlives any wording change to ``error``. Adding
one is a change to 08 and to the TypeScript mirror, never to this
module alone.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

EventName.description:
Every event name in the vocabulary, one member per row of 03.

Values are ``subject.verb``. Adding one is a change to 03 and to the
TypeScript mirror, never to this module alone.
EventName.title: EventName

GraphBranch.description:
The tasks of one node that belong to one branch of a fan-out.

``from_task`` is the fan-out that produced the branch — the
``lineage.from`` of the first task in the branch chain whose parent
returned a list — and is ``null`` for a node reached by a single path,
which has exactly one branch.

from_task.description: The fan-out task this branch came out of.
from_task.title: From Task

tasks.description: This node's attempts in that branch, oldest first.
tasks.title: Tasks

GraphBranch.title: GraphBranch

GraphEdge.description:
One arrow of the finalized graph, and how often this run took it.

``from`` is a Python keyword, so the field is ``from_`` and carries
``from`` as its alias — the name 08 fixes on the wire.

kind.description: Forward, a loop back, or an arrow into a join.

traversed.description: How often this run took the edge: `task.enqueued reason=transition` between the two nodes, plus `join.arrived` for a join edge.
traversed.title: Traversed

GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge

GraphNode.description: One node of the graph, with this run's history on it.

arrivals.description: For a join with a fan-out still open, how much of it has arrived; absent otherwise.

attempts.description: How many task rows this node has in this run.
attempts.title: Attempts

branches.description: The node's tasks grouped by the fan-out that produced them.
branches.title: Branches

generation.description: BFS depth from the start node.
generation.title: Generation

join.description: Whether the node waits for a fan-out to complete.
join.title: Join

last_task_id.description: The highest task id of the node, the one the task drawer opens; null when the node has no task.
last_task_id.title: Last Task Id

live.description: Whether a `node`-slot plugin panel should show: the node is in progress or waiting, or it has at least one done attempt (09 §Slots).
live.title: Live

state.description: What the node is doing, by 08's precedence.

GraphNode.title: GraphNode

edges.description: Every edge of the finalized graph.
edges.title: Edges

Health.description: Liveness, version and counts. Unauthenticated, and carries no ids.

ok.description: True whenever the server answers at all.
ok.title: Ok

pools.description: Every registered pool by name. Omitted when this application has no engine; empty when the engine has no pools.
pools.title: Pools

runs_running.description: Runs in the `running` status. Omitted when this application has no store to ask.
runs_running.title: Runs Running

tasks_in_progress.description: Attempts in the `in_progress` status; a task parked on a human is `waiting` and is not counted. Omitted when this application has no store to ask.
tasks_in_progress.title: Tasks In Progress

Health.title: Health

JoinArrived.description:
One per branch reaching a join.

``arrived == count`` means the join task was enqueued in the same
transaction.
JoinArrived.title: JoinArrived

LogAppended.description: ``preview`` is the first 200 characters of the entry.
LogAppended.title: LogAppended

LogEntry.description:
One entry of a run's work log, append-only (03).

The work log is the inter-stage channel (D4): the engine's failures,
the operator's notes and every agent deliverable, in one ordered list.
``kind`` is absent on a plain entry.

id.description: The entry id; the log is ordered by it.
id.title: Id

kind.description: What it is, for filtering; absent on a plain entry.

node.description: The node it was written under; `user` for an operator note with no node in flight.
node.title: Node

run_id.description: The run the entry belongs to.
run_id.title: Run Id

task_id.description: The attempt that wrote it, when one did.
task_id.title: Task Id

LogEntry.title: LogEntry

LogKind.description:
What a work-log entry is, for filtering (the agent view drops
``stats``; 08 §Agent-facing).
LogKind.title: LogKind

LogRef.description: The id of a work-log entry that was appended (08 §Runs).

log_id.description: The id of the entry that was written.
log_id.title: Log Id

LogRef.title: LogRef

LogText.description: Append an entry to a run's work log (`POST /api/runs/{id}/log`).

text.description: The entry, written verbatim and never truncated.
text.title: Text

LogText.title: LogText

Me.description: What the caller may do, and which server they are talking to.

auth.description: `token` when operator endpoints require a bearer token, `off` on a plain loopback bind.
auth.title: Auth

authenticated.description: Whether this request carries operator rights. Always true when `auth` is `off`.
authenticated.title: Authenticated

features.description: Optional capabilities this server has. Empty in v1.
features.title: Features

started_at.description: When this process came up. A change means a restart, which is the SPA's cue to refetch the plugin manifest.
started_at.title: Started At

Me.title: Me

Move.description: Move a task's work to another node (`POST /api/tasks/{id}/move`).

node.description: The node to enqueue the work at.
node.title: Node

Move.title: Move

NewRun.description:
Submit a run of a workflow (`POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs`).

The two fields become the start task's payload, which is why editing
either afterwards does not rewrite it (04 §Submit a run).

description.description: Longer context for the run; the workflow's input.
description.title: Description

title.description: The operator's title for the run.
title.title: Title

NewRun.title: NewRun

NodeOut.description:
One node's edges and its options, as 08 §Workflows lists them.

``priority`` and ``retries`` of ``null`` mean "the server default"
and ``timeout`` of ``null`` means no wall-clock cap on one attempt —
the node metadata of 04 §Node options, unresolved, because what the
default *is* belongs to the settings of the server running it.

description.description: The body's docstring, unless the node overrode it.
description.title: Description

edges.description: The nodes this one may transition to, in declaration order.
edges.title: Edges

generation.description: BFS depth from the start node; a loop-back edge targets a generation at or below its source.
generation.title: Generation

label.description: The display name; the function's name by default.
label.title: Label

priority.description: Dispatch priority, or null for the server default.
priority.title: Priority

retries.description: Retry budget, or null for the server default.
retries.title: Retries

timeout.description: Seconds one attempt may run, or null for no cap.
timeout.title: Timeout

NodeOut.title: NodeOut

NodeState.description:
What a node is doing in one run, in 08 §Graph semantics' precedence.

Declared in precedence order, highest first, so the rule is the
member order and not a table kept somewhere else. ``failed`` outranks
``done`` but is itself outranked by ``ready``: a failed attempt whose
retry is queued reports ``ready``, because that retry row exists and
the node is going to run again. ``idle`` means no task of this node
was ever created in this run.

The SPA colours by this alone (10 §Status colours).
NodeState.title: NodeState

Ok.description:
An operation that succeeded and has nothing else to report.

``note`` is the one place a router adds a sentence about *how* it
succeeded — 08 §Runs' `{ok, note?}` — and is omitted when there is
nothing to say rather than sent as an empty string.

note.description: What was unusual about the success, when anything was.
note.title: Note

ok.description: Always true; a failure is an error body.
ok.title: Ok

Ok.title: Ok

PanelKind.description:
The renderer vocabulary of 09 §Panel kinds, one member per row.

The kind fixes the shape ``source`` must return: ``markdown`` a
string, ``kv`` an object, ``table`` ``{columns, rows}``, ``log`` a
list of entries, ``chart`` ``{series, kind}``, ``dashboard``
``{note?, metrics, table?}``, ``form`` the name of an action, and
``custom`` nothing at all — the plugin's own web component reads what
it needs through ``window.athanore``.

A kind the SPA does not know renders a placeholder card rather than
crashing the pane (09), so this enum is the server's vocabulary and
not a promise about the browser's.
PanelKind.title: PanelKind

PanelOut.description:
One panel of the manifest (09 §Wire contract).

``source`` is the mounted URL of the route the panel's data comes
from, or — for a ``form`` panel — the name of the action whose model
is the form. ``node`` is present only on a panel that follows one;
whether that node is *live* travels on the run's graph rather than
here, because the manifest changes only on restart (08 §Graph
semantics).

element.description: The custom element tag a `custom` panel renders.
element.title: Element

kind.description: Which renderer draws it, and its data shape.

name.description: The panel's title, unique within its workflow.
name.title: Name

node.description: The node this panel follows, when it follows one.
node.title: Node

placement.description: A pane of its own, or a card on the run overview.
placement.title: Placement

refresh_on.description: Event-name globs that invalidate this panel's data.
refresh_on.title: Refresh On

scope.description: What has to be resolved before it can load.

source.description: The URL its data comes from, or the action name for a form.
source.title: Source

PanelOut.title: PanelOut

PluginEvent.description:
``plugin.<workflow>.<name>``: the vocabulary's open end.

The handler's data is free-form, so the wire carries whatever it passed
to ``ctx.services.events.publish``; 18 requires a JSON object, and the
registry — not this model — enforces that ``<workflow>`` is the
publishing workflow.

``name`` is the only one in the union that is not a
:class:`~typing.Literal`, and it is declared as the whole vocabulary
— ``EventName | str`` — rather than as a bare ``str``. The two are
the same set of strings, so nothing is widened; what the wider
spelling buys is a *reference* to the enum in the generated document,
which is where 08 §OpenAPI wants the event-name enum published and
where the SPA's TypeScript union is generated from (13 §Contract
tests). The validator below is what actually narrows this field, to
the ``plugin.`` namespace.
PluginEvent.title: PluginEvent

PluginManifestEntry.description: What one workflow contributes to the UI (09 §Wire contract).

assets.description: URLs of the JavaScript modules the SPA injects for it.
assets.title: Assets

workflow.description: The workflow that declared these, or `_builtin` for the views the core ships.
workflow.title: Workflow

PluginManifestEntry.title: PluginManifestEntry

PoolHealth.description: One pool's capacity and what it is spending right now.

capacity.description: Slots the pool has, in total.
capacity.title: Capacity

PoolHealth.title: PoolHealth

Position.description:
Move a run in the dispatch list (`POST /api/runs/{id}/position`, D57).

Exactly one of the two. ``direction`` swaps with the neighbour above
(``-1``) or below (``+1``) and is a no-op at the ends — still a 200,
reporting the position the run already had. ``index`` is the
**zero-based** list index to move to, clamped to the list; New Run's
"top" is `{"index": 0}` and "bottom" is the default, which needs no
call at all.

direction.description: Swap with the neighbour above (-1) or below (1).
direction.title: Direction

index.description: The zero-based list index to move to, clamped.
index.title: Index

Position.title: Position

PositionOut.description: Where a run sits in the dispatch list after a move (D57).

position.description: The run's place in the dispatch list after the move, numbered from 1. The `index` that asked for it is zero-based (D57).
position.title: Position

PositionOut.title: PositionOut

RequestAnswered.description: ``value`` is not in the event (may be large or sensitive); fetch it.
RequestAnswered.title: RequestAnswered

RequestKind.description: What the request is about. A label for the UI; nothing keys on it.
RequestKind.title: RequestKind

RequestMode.description: The shape of the answer a request expects (06 §The model).
RequestMode.title: RequestMode

RequestOption.description:
One choice an ``options`` request offers (06 §The model).

The agent's options verbatim for an ACP permission: the operator
picks under the labels the agent used, and the ``option_id`` that
goes back is the one it will be given (05 §Policies).

kind.description: The ACP permission kind, when the option came from one.
kind.title: Kind

RequestOption.title: RequestOption

RequestSource.description: Who raised the request: the agent mid-turn, or the node body.
RequestSource.title: RequestSource

RequestView.description:
A request, its answer, and the node that asked (08 §Requests).

``schema`` is spelled ``schema_`` in Python — a field named ``schema``
shadows an attribute of ``BaseModel`` — and keeps ``schema`` as its
alias, which is the name 08 fixes on the wire.

age.description: Seconds since it was opened, when it was read.
age.title: Age

answer.description: The chosen `option_id`, or the value of a `text` or `form` answer. Null both before an answer and for an answer that was null.
answer.title: Answer

answered_by.description: Who answered; the field to test for having an answer at all.

kind.description: What the request is about; a label.

mode.description: The shape of the answer expected.

pending.description: Unanswered, with an attempt still waiting.
pending.title: Pending

prompt.description: What the operator is being asked.
prompt.title: Prompt

schema.description: The JSON Schema the answer must fit, for a `form` request.
schema.title: Schema

source.description: Whether the agent asked mid-turn or the node body did.

stale.description: Unanswered, with no attempt left to consume an answer: in history, out of the inbox, and no longer answerable.
stale.title: Stale

tool_call.description: What the agent was about to do, for a permission request.
tool_call.title: Tool Call

RequestView.title: RequestView

Rerun.description:
Run a node again (`POST /api/runs/{id}/rerun`).

The payload and branch it last had are re-used; a rerun of a join
replays the arrivals it fired on (04 §Operator operations).
Rerun.title: Rerun

RunChanges.description: The fields an edit or an op changed on a run; only those it changed.
RunChanges.title: RunChanges

RunCompleted.description:
``output`` follows the shape rule of 04 §Routing edge cases.

``node`` and ``task_id`` are the last landing task. ``output`` is
required and may be ``null``: a body that returns ``None`` terminates
the run with that value, which is not the same as an unknown one.
RunCompleted.title: RunCompleted

RunDeleted.description: The last event of a run: it is deleted with the run, so SSE only.
RunDeleted.title: RunDeleted

RunDetail.description: A run, its tasks and its totals (08 §Runs).

current_nodes.description: The nodes with an in-progress or waiting attempt right now.
current_nodes.title: Current Nodes

output.description: The run's output: one value for a single terminal task, a list in branch order when several branches terminated (D58). Null before the run ends, and also when it ended by returning null.
output.title: Output

outputs.description: One entry per terminal task, always a list (D58).
outputs.title: Outputs

pending_requests.description: Unanswered, non-stale requests waiting on a person.
pending_requests.title: Pending Requests

position.description: The run's place in the dispatch list; runs are numbered 1..n in list order.
position.title: Position

stats.description: The agent totals of the run.

tasks.description: Every attempt of the run, oldest first.
tasks.title: Tasks

title.description: The operator's title for the run.
title.title: Title

unregistered.description: Whether this server has no workflow of that name registered.
unregistered.title: Unregistered

updated.description: When anything about it last changed.
updated.title: Updated

RunDetail.title: RunDetail

RunFailed.description: ``code`` is set when the run stalled on a partial join.
RunFailed.title: RunFailed

RunOutput.description: One terminal task's value, with the branch it came out of (D58).

branch.description: The fan-out stack the attempt was inside, outermost first; empty for a run that never fanned out.
branch.title: Branch

task_id.description: The terminal attempt that produced it.
task_id.title: Task Id

RunOutput.title: RunOutput

RunStarted.description: The first claim of the run.
RunStarted.title: RunStarted

RunStats.description:
A run's agent totals, summed over its attempts (05 §Stats).

Every field is optional and nothing is zero-filled: a provider that
reported no cost leaves ``cost`` absent rather than claiming zero (01
§Real data only). ``duration_s`` is the sum of the attempts' durations
and not wall-clock time, which fan-out would make meaningless.
RunStats.title: RunStats

RunStatus.description:
The run state machine of 03.

``queued`` is new in v1: a run that exists but has dispatched nothing,
so "waiting for a slot" is visible. The three terminal states are
re-openable by retry, rerun and move.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

RunSummary.description:
One row of the run list (08 §Runs).

``current_nodes`` is plural because a fan-out puts a run in several
nodes at once. ``unregistered`` is not stored: it says this server has
no workflow of that name registered, so the run is shown but nothing
will dispatch it (03 §Run).

current_nodes.description: The nodes with an in-progress or waiting attempt right now.
current_nodes.title: Current Nodes

pending_requests.description: Unanswered, non-stale requests waiting on a person.
pending_requests.title: Pending Requests

position.description: The run's place in the dispatch list; runs are numbered 1..n in list order.
position.title: Position

title.description: The operator's title for the run.
title.title: Title

unregistered.description: Whether this server has no workflow of that name registered.
unregistered.title: Unregistered

updated.description: When anything about it last changed.
updated.title: Updated

RunSummary.title: RunSummary

SetStatus.description:
Write one of the three statuses an operator may set (08 §Tasks).

The other four are the engine's own record of what happened and are
not an operator's to declare.

status.description: `ready` re-dispatches the task, `cancelled` stops it, `dead_letter` files it as failed for good.
status.title: Status

SetStatus.title: SetStatus

get.description:
Everything the agent needs to start, and nothing else (08).

The title and the description are the run's — the brief an operator
submitted — and ``input`` is the payload this node was enqueued with,
``null`` when it had none. ``log`` is the run's work log, oldest
first, uncapped and untruncated: it is the inter-stage channel (D4),
it is bounded by the number of stages rather than by agent output,
and a retried attempt reads the ``failure`` entry that says why the
last one failed.

The ``stats`` entries are dropped (D56). ``output_schema`` is here
only while a façade has declared an ``output_model`` on this
attempt's live context: the ``native`` tooling tier reads it to build
its ``submit_result`` tool (05 §Tooling tiers), and an agent with no
model declared is not required to submit anything.

post.description:
Open a request against this attempt, if the agent may ask at all.

403 unless the façade running this attempt declared
``ask_policy="http"`` (05 §Policies): an agent cannot grant itself
the right to interrupt a person, and the policy lives on the agent
class the workflow chose. The prompt sections that tell an agent how
to ask are omitted when it is off (19), so a 403 here is an agent
that went looking.

What was sent decides the mode: ``options`` for a pick-one question,
``schema`` for a form — whose answer is validated against that very
schema where it lands, by the validator registered here (06
§Service) — and neither for free text. The request is opened with
``source="agent"`` and no ordinal, because a re-executed attempt does
not reproduce a turn statement for statement (06 §Restart
durability).

The answer does not come back here: the caller polls
``/requests/{rid}``, which is what lets the agent keep its turn
rather than holding this connection open.

get.description:
The answer, waiting up to ``wait`` seconds for one to land.

``wait`` is clamped to :data:`MAX_WAIT` rather than refused, so 19's
instruction — poll with ``?wait=60`` and repeat until it says
``answered`` — is a loop that costs one request per minute and not a
spin. The wait ends the moment the answer is recorded, not when the
clamp expires.

A request of **another** task is a 404, not someone else's answer: a
token names one attempt and this route reads only what that attempt
opened (12 §Task tokens).

Nothing is claimed. An agent that lost a response and asked again
gets the same answer again, which is what makes a dropped connection
cost nothing (06 §Service).

post.description:
Record a value for this attempt, if it fits what was asked for.

With an ``output_model`` declared, a misfit is a 422 carrying
``errors`` and ``schema`` and nothing is stored: the agent reads the
two in its own tool output and can fix the shape inside the same turn
(05 §Submissions). The rejection is also left on the context as
``ctx.last_rejection``, which is what 19's repair turn quotes back if
the turn ends without a valid submission.

With none declared, any JSON is stored as it arrived.

Submitting twice is not an error: the **latest valid** payload wins
(D5), and a body reads it with ``submissions.latest()``. A submission
never routes anything — the node body decides — so an agent cannot
move its own task.

post.description:
Put the task in one of the three statuses an operator may write.

``ready`` re-dispatches it and re-opens a terminal run, ``cancelled``
stops it and ``dead_letter`` files it as failed for good; the other
four statuses are the engine's record of what happened and are not an
operator's to declare, which is why the body's field is a
``Literal`` and a fourth value is a 422 before the engine is reached.

get.description:
The module a workflow's nodes are defined in, and their line numbers.

The file is the one the **start node's** body is defined in — the
module the author wrote the workflow in — and ``nodes`` carries a line
for each node whose body is defined in that same file. A node whose
function was imported from elsewhere is left out rather than given a
line into text that does not contain it (01 §Real data only).

A workflow whose source Python cannot produce — a body built by
``exec``, or one whose file has been deleted since import — is a 404:
the workflow is registered, but this view of it does not exist.
